briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
An Israeli airstrike in Beirut's Dahiyeh district, targeting Hezbollah infrastructure, has severely jeopardized an imminent US-Iran peace deal, drawing sharp condemnation from US President Trump. This strike has triggered immediate threats of retaliation from Iran's IRGC, prompting Israel to declare a nationwide high alert for potential missile attacks. Diplomatic efforts are intensely focused on preventing a wider regional escalation.

IRAN
President Pezeshkian stated that problems with Gulf states are nearing resolution and that the government is united on defending national interests through negotiation, emphasizing that the Supreme Leader and National Security Council determine war and negotiation. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf declared that the Israeli strike in Dahiyeh proved the US lacks the will or ability to fulfill its commitments, rendering further negotiations "impossible." Similarly, Mohammad Marandi, a member of the negotiating team, stated "no further negotiations will be underway." IRGC-affiliated sources and Khatam al-Anbiya's Deputy Commander Mohammad Jafar Assadi vowed that Israeli "crimes" in Beirut would not go unanswered, with threats of a "rain of missiles" on Israel before dawn tomorrow.

Amidst these threats, a senior Iranian official, via Reuters, outlined terms of a draft US-Iran memorandum: US agrees to release $25 billion in frozen assets, waive oil sanctions for a specified period, and allow Iran to dilute its highly enriched uranium stockpile inside Iran. In return, Iran would commit not to produce or acquire nuclear weapons and immediately reopen the Strait of Hormuz to all commercial vessels. However, Iranian TV and Fars News reported the Strait of Hormuz remains closed to foreign vessels, a claim contradicted by the US Secretary of Defense.

Internally, four major Iranian banks experienced a limited cyberattack that disrupted services, though no customer data was compromised. Hardline elements have protested the potential US-Iran deal, accusing negotiators Qalibaf and Araghchi of making "great concessions" and "selling out" the "blood of my leader," suggesting a lack of approval from Mojtaba Khamenei. The Intelligence Ministry announced the arrest of dozens of "terrorists, spies, and saboteurs" during the recent US-Israeli aggression.

ISRAEL
The IDF conducted a "precise" airstrike in Beirut's Dahiyeh district, targeting a Hezbollah headquarters and infrastructure used to advance terror attacks against Israeli civilians and forces. The strike involved two fighter jets and four precision munitions, killing 2-3 individuals and injuring 7-15. This operation was in response to three Hezbollah drones launched into northern Israel earlier today.

The IDF confirmed the killing of senior Hezbollah commander Ali Mussa Daqduq in southern Lebanon over the weekend. Daqduq, a commander in the elite Radwan Force and head of the "Golan File," was also responsible for Hassan Nasrallah's security and was previously imprisoned by US forces in 2007 for orchestrating the killing of five American soldiers in Iraq. Another senior Hezbollah commander, Ali al-Haj (head of Hezbollah's communications unit), was reported killed in the Dahiyeh strike.

Following the Beirut strike, IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir held urgent assessments, stating the IDF is prepared for potential Iranian missile fire "in the coming hours" and "will not tolerate fire toward the territory of the State of Israel." Zamir also approved new battle plans for Lebanon, designating it as Israel's "main center of gravity."

The Home Front Command implemented new nationwide gathering restrictions, limiting events to 5,000 people (no change for border communities, remaining at 100 outdoors/400 indoors), and police raised national alert levels. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's security cabinet is set to convene tonight. US President Trump conveyed his "very unhappy" message to Netanyahu regarding the Beirut strike, criticizing Netanyahu's "no fucking judgment." Netanyahu, however, affirmed Israel's right to self-defense but stated no further attacks should occur in Lebanon. Defense Minister Israel Katz appointed Brig. Gen. Hisham Ibrahim, a senior Druze officer, as his military secretary.

Gaza envelope communities (Kfar Azza, Zimrat, Shuva, Sa'ad) experienced rocket alerts. In the West Bank, 5 individuals were killed in Israeli attacks in Jabalia, and Israeli forces stormed towns, abducting Palestinians. Settlers vandalized Palestinian vehicles and property near Qalqilya.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Rocket alerts were activated in Israeli communities bordering Gaza, including Kfar Azza, Zimrat, Shuva, and Sa'ad. In the Gaza Strip, reports indicate 5 fatalities from Israeli attacks in Jabalia, North Gaza. In the occupied West Bank, Israeli forces conducted multiple overnight raids, storming towns and abducting several Palestinians. Israeli settlers were reported to have vandalized Palestinian vehicles and property in the village of Jit, near Qalqilya.

LEBANON
Hezbollah continued cross-border operations, launching three drones into northern Israel, which reportedly struck military zones without causing injuries. Rocket fire targeted Metula, and an Ababil attack drone was used against an IDF Merkava tank near Beaufort Castle. Hezbollah also reported targeting Israeli military gatherings in Al-Qantara and Naqoura, and a logistical point in Al-Bayyada, with attack drones and "qualitative missiles."

Israel launched a significant airstrike on a Hezbollah headquarters and infrastructure in Beirut's Dahiyeh district, resulting in 2-3 deaths and 7-15 injuries. This strike followed the killing of senior Hezbollah commander Ali Mussa Daqduq in southern Lebanon on Friday and reportedly Ali al-Haj, head of Hezbollah's communications unit, in the Beirut strike. Israeli artillery shelled southern towns like Majdal Zoun and al-Mansouri, and Israeli forces are advancing in the area near Beaufort Castle, dismantling Hezbollah tunnel systems. The IDF issued evacuation warnings for 29 villages in southern Lebanon ahead of further strikes.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Ali Mussa Daqduq, a senior Hezbollah commander killed by Israel, previously commanded the "Golan File," an operational branch responsible for Hezbollah's entrenchment efforts in southern Syria. He was also involved in activities in Iraq and was imprisoned by US forces in 2007 for orchestrating the kidnapping and murder of five American soldiers there. In Iraq, the 12th anniversary of the Al-Jihad Al-Kifa'i fatwa was commemorated, with calls to limit arms to state institutions. The director of the SOMO oil company stated no Iraqi oil tankers were targeted during the recent US-Iran escalation.

GULF STATES
Iranian President Pezeshkian indicated that "many issues and misunderstandings" with Gulf states are "on the way to resolution." Qatar is actively mediating between the US and Iran, with Qatari negotiators traveling to Tehran to finalize the potential agreement. Anwar Gargash, diplomatic advisor to the UAE President, expressed hope that the impending US-Iran agreement will "turn the page of war" and open a successful political path. Kuwait announced the withdrawal of citizenship from 2193 individuals.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Israeli airstrike in Beirut's Dahiyeh:** Israel conducted a "precise" airstrike on Hezbollah headquarters and infrastructure in Beirut's Dahiyeh district, responding to Hezbollah drone attacks; the strike resulted in 2-3 deaths and 7-15 injuries.
2.  **Killing of Senior Hezbollah Commanders:** Israel confirmed the elimination of Ali Mussa Daqduq in southern Lebanon and reportedly Ali al-Haj in Beirut, both senior Hezbollah figures with significant operational roles.
3.  **Trump's Outrage over Beirut Strike:** US President Trump vehemently criticized Netanyahu, claiming the Beirut strike "made me very angry" and jeopardized an imminent US-Iran peace deal slated for signing today.
4.  **Iranian Threats of Retaliation and Halting Negotiations:** IRGC-affiliated sources threatened an immediate "rain of missiles" on Israel, while Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf declared US-Iran negotiations "impossible" after the Dahiyeh strike, accusing the US of bad faith.
5.  **IDF on High Alert:** The IDF raised its alert level for potential Iranian missile fire, implemented nationwide gathering restrictions (max 5,000 people), and Chief of Staff Zamir approved new battle plans focusing on Lebanon as the "main center of gravity."
6.  **Details of Draft US-Iran Deal Emerge:** A senior Iranian official disclosed that the draft memorandum includes US agreement to release $25 billion in frozen Iranian assets, waive oil sanctions, and allow uranium enrichment dilution in Iran, in exchange for Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and not acquiring nuclear weapons.
7.  **Conflicting Strait of Hormuz Status:** Iranian TV reported the Strait of Hormuz as closed to foreign vessels, directly contradicting US Secretary of Defense Hegseth's claim of US control over the waterway.
8.  **Internal Iranian Dissent:** Hardline groups in Iran protested the potential US-Iran agreement, accusing chief negotiators Qalibaf and Araghchi of "betrayal" and acting without the Supreme Leader's full endorsement.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The immediate threat of direct Iranian retaliation against Israel is assessed as high, with both the IDF and IRGC-affiliated sources indicating a potential response in the "coming hours." This poses a significant escalation risk, potentially drawing the region into wider conflict. Active flashpoints include the northern Israeli border, where Hezbollah continues drone and rocket attacks, and southern Lebanon, where Israeli ground forces are advancing and conducting strikes, with evacuation warnings issued for 29 villages. The fate of the US-Iran deal remains highly volatile; its collapse could remove a critical diplomatic off-ramp, while its perceived "betrayal" by Iranian hardliners could further destabilize Iran's internal political landscape. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical choke point, with conflicting reports on its status exacerbating tensions. A cyberattack on Iranian banks highlights potential new domains of conflict.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
US President Donald Trump strongly condemned Israel's strike in Beirut, expressing extreme displeasure with Prime Minister Netanyahu and stating the attack jeopardized an imminent US-Iran deal. Trump reiterated calls for de-escalation from all parties but maintained optimism that the deal would still be signed today. US Secretary of Defense Hegseth stated the deal is a "question of when, not if" and urged Iran to curb Hezbollah, while US Ambassador to the UN Mike Welch affirmed Trump's commitment to the agreement. US diplomats also reportedly accused Israel of trying to "sabotage the President's deal" and drag the US back into war. Former President Obama suggested the new deal is not fundamentally different from the JCPOA and stressed the need for diplomacy over military solutions.

Russia's President Putin, in a call with Trump, expressed satisfaction with de-escalation efforts with Iran. Qatar is actively mediating, with a negotiation team traveling to Tehran to finalize the deal. Pakistan is also reported as a mediator. The UAE's diplomatic advisor, Anwar Gargash, hoped the agreement would "turn the page of war." UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer ordered British forces to intercept a "shadow fleet" Russian oil tanker in the English Channel, an action unrelated to the Middle East but indicative of broader international tensions. Jordan reported false alarms for rocket fire due to technical issues.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding the US-Iran deal. President Trump announced the deal would be signed "today" (June 14) or "tomorrow" (June 15), while Iranian officials (Foreign Ministry, Parliament Speaker Qalibaf, negotiator Marandi) explicitly stated that no signing would occur today and that negotiations were halted. Furthermore, the Iranian TV and Fars News reported the Strait of Hormuz is closed, directly conflicting with US Defense Secretary Hegseth's assertion that the US maintains control.

Casualty figures from the Beirut strike also vary, with initial Lebanese reports citing 1 killed and 4 injured, later updated to 2 killed and 7 injured, and then 3 killed and 15 injured.

A highly unverified and potentially propagandistic claim by Press TV alleged "US use of AI in Iran elementary school massacre" during a previous "US-Israeli aggression," with Anthropic's CEO reportedly denying breach of "red lines." This claim lacks independent corroboration and should be treated with extreme caution. Similarly, Iranian IRGC-affiliated channels' threats of "rain of missiles" are indicative of propaganda, aiming to bolster domestic resolve and project strength.

A major contradiction comes from @mamlekate, which reports that Ali Khamenei was killed "over 100 days ago" and that his funeral plans are now being announced. This stands in stark contrast to all other sources, which discuss Khamenei's political and military decisions as if he is alive and active. This contradiction merits further investigation into its origin and veracity.

Reporting gaps include the full and independently confirmed text of the draft US-Iran deal and the specific identity of the "very senior Israeli official" quoted as calling the deal "shit." The motivations behind some internal Iranian hardline protests against the deal, beyond general anti-US sentiment, are also not fully detailed.
